value.body: A policy analyst researches public issues, laws and programmes, and writes analysis that helps governments and organisations make decisions. Think tanks, government departments and programmes, NGOs, international agencies and consultancies hire them. A day involves reading reports, analysing data, interviewing stakeholders and writing briefs.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: BA in Political Science, Economics or Sociology; often a master's

items.label: Common tools
items.value: Excel or Stata/R, government data portals, report writing

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Freshers often start through research internships, fellowships or research-assistant posts at think tanks, NGOs and government programmes. A master's degree in public policy, economics or development is common for longer-term roles.

value.title: Skills you'll use
items: Reading laws, budgets and government data

value.title: At a glance
items: Many entry roles are fixed-term fellowships or project contracts.
Common next roles: senior analyst, programme manager, policy advisor.
Published writing and a track record of research matter for growth.
